Near-misses that were just as close were discarded: E054 (-0.06 below the gate), E061 (-0.04), E044 (-0.03). Keeping whatever clears 0.753 on the same three fixed seeds selects upward, so the tip's expected mean on new seeds is probably at or below 0.753. H4.1.2 and H4.1.5 (extra-seed checks in drafts/) were proposed early and never run. Every 'keep' decision since E041 has been made without them.
critiques.suggestion: Before any more time cuts, evaluate E058 offline on seeds 3-12, and E048 too if the budget allows. If the extra-seed mean is below ~0.753, spend the next runs on recovering margin, not on speed. Freeze the keep rule until this is measured.

But E057 is a single draw: three per-seed deltas from one RNG shift. You cannot estimate an sd from that. It also conflicts with the E044 vs E048 gap (-0.23 vs +0.02 for the same 28 px stage, about 4 sd under the E057 model). Either that gap was a real interaction (20 px x 28 px, or head lr x2), or the E057 sd is too low. After E057 the notebook started tightening bands to ±0.12 pp. Those bands rest on one sample.
critiques.suggestion: Run 2-3 more RNG-shift edits offline (different dummy-draw counts) on the tip to get an actual sd. Update H4 and H4.1 to a single number and set H4.1.4 to supported or inconclusive based on that. Until then, treat every |delta| < 0.25 pp as inconclusive. That includes the exchange rates computed from such deltas.

critiques.target: E063 surprise (+0.25 epoch bought only +0.07 pp)
critiques.issue: This contradicts the ~1.14 pp/epoch slope used to motivate H5, E037, E040 and I081. Possible explanations, none tested: (a) noise, since the comparison is a single run against E061, itself a single run; (b) the freeze points and the lookahead (t/T)^3 ramp moved with the stretched schedule, so the change was not 'just +0.25 epoch'; (c) the curriculum plus freeze really did flatten the 32 px tail. structured_output.summary:
The biggest risk is the margin. The tip E058 clears the gate by 0.07 pp, reached by keeping three noise-sized changes (E051, E052, E058) while discarding equally close near-misses (E044, E054, E061). The extra-seed checks proposed long ago (H4.1.2, H4.1.5) have never been run, so the tip's real mean on new seeds is unknown and probably at or below 0.753.

The noise model is unresolved. E057's ~0.06 pp sd comes from a single draw and conflicts with the E044 vs E048 gap, yet many lines were closed or prioritised on exchange rates whose numerators are within that noise.

The results contradict H1. Every 'update-side lever left' it named lost 0.26-1.5 pp, and its time target was met by a freeze. H6 does not explain why late per-block freezing is cheap (E058), why the early phase is step-starved (E053), or why the marginal 32 px epoch was suddenly worth only ~0.3 pp (E063). That last result implies an epoch cut on the current base may be cheap, and it has not been tested.

E065's -1.5 pp makes the NS2 'systems' ideas risky. Its own closure also depends on an unreported check that the update norms actually matched.

H1.6.6 suggests the lookahead change in E028 may never have taken effect, so the tip may not be running the setting the tree describes. Statuses and evidence tokens are out of date across about 10 nodes.

Recommended order: the extra-seed margin check, E058 at 6.5 epochs, the compile no-op check, the trial-0 timing-leak check, a max-autotune re-check, then cheap single-scalar probes (BN-bias x32, NS4).
